PART III  Nutrition in the Life Cycle
CLINICAL CASE STUDY
MF is an 86-year-old Caucasian female resident in a skilled nursing facility 
with unintentional weight loss. She was admitted 3 months ago from the 
hospital after a hip fracture. She had been residing in an independent 
living facility for several years. She reports she has been eating poorly 
because of difficulty moving around, being generally uncomfortable, and 
states, “If I am not active I don’t need to eat so much.” Intake is less than 
50% of regular diet. No problems chewing or swallowing are noted after 
a speech language pathologist’s evaluation. Admission weight was 112 
pounds; current weight is 95 pounds. Self-reported height is 5’3”; Hgb/
Hct, normal; total cholesterol, 135; and Mini Nutrition Assessment score,
